velocity_color_scale.meaning: Adaptive continuous diverging display scale for observed vertical velocity. Zero is the physical divider: negative/subsidence is red and positive/uplift is blue. The symmetric near-zero band is derived from P75 of 2 sigma_up; negative and positive P98 limits are determined independently and clipped only for display. Display limits are contrast controls, not hazard thresholds.

geometry.meaning: One shared low-poly checkerboard mesh is instanced per measured RUM only. Position/scale update each epoch; mesh geometry is not rebuilt. Blankies remain flat translucent support without uncertainty relief. Amplitude-aware tint fading keeps low/zero relief visually clean.

facet_tint.meaning: Unlit, hue-safe luminance multipliers for full-strength relief. Upward facets retain a subtle cue; downward facets are intentionally fainter. Low-amplitude RUMs blend both back toward 1.0, so the scientific mean colour stays dominant and zero relief is visually clean.

lod.meaning: Automatic semantic LOD for measured-RUM uncertainty relief. At overview scale the renderer instances a sparse 2x2 checkerboard; at close inspection it switches to 4x4. Each 2x2 pyramid keeps the same physical base size as a 4x4 pyramid, so overview mode is sparser rather than larger. The RUM footprint must be at least near_min_cell_pixels wide before moving to 4x4, and it must shrink below far_max_cell_pixels before returning to 2x2. The two thresholds create hysteresis so small zoom changes do not repeatedly rebuild layers. High-pitch views force 2x2 as a performance safeguard.
lod.grazing_pitch_force_far_meaning: At or above this pitch, force the sparse 2x2 relief mesh even when zoom alone would choose 4x4. This prevents horizon-angle relief overdraw.

uncertaintyRelief.note: unit=sigma means a multiple of each cell's current sigma; unit=mm means a fixed absolute future relief range. The renderer instances one static checkerboard mesh per cell; no per-epoch cap geometry is rebuilt.

horizontalStaticGlyphs.purpose: Proto1 RUM horizontal arrow / covariance-ellipse math prepared for native DeckGL instancing. Arrow tail is the RUM coordinate and the confidence ellipse is centred at the vector tip. Observed RUMs only; no blankie horizontal interpolation.

history.storage: RGBA32F texture: local_x_m, local_y_m, particle_age_s, speed_ratio_to_p95 (uncapped; visual alpha/width outputs clamp)
history.rationale: Fixed simulation-time cadence makes visible trail duration independent of display frame rate. Trail alpha uses V7-style exponential canvas persistence; age resets mark respawn discontinuities; Z is recomputed from current vertical model at draw time. Requested duration reallocates only the sentinel-filled history target and never reseeds particle simulation state. At high visual speed, metric substeps validate support across the path and the screen-jump guard suppresses any remaining misleading cross-map connector.

atlas.rationale: Runtime tiles particle columns into multiple rows before multiplying by history samples, avoiding an excessively wide RGBA32F target while keeping texelFetch history reads exact.

horizontalParticleLsc.purpose: Optional least-squares-collocation horizontal deformation signal field. Raw estimates remain available unchanged as a separate particle flow-field mode.

sampling.rule: Fine LSC texture sampled through the existing conservative-v1 shader rule. Fine texels are valid only where their nearest coarse RUM is observed; no blank/no-data prediction is emitted.

spawnDomain.rule: same raw eight-neighbour-supported coarse emitter set, re-expressed in fine-grid coordinates
spawnDomain.fallback: all above-stall live RUMs only when no supported emitter cells exist

lscModel.variogramFitWeightingMeaning: Equal weight per populated empirical semivariogram bin. This is reference-locked because it reproduces the Jakarta validation parameters provided with the LSC handoff; pair counts remain recorded for audit.
lscModel.forcedImmediateNeighbourPolicy: parent plus all available live Moore-8 neighbours are retained before distance ranking.
lscModel.fixedNeighbourTradeoff: Fixed parent-cell neighbour membership reuses two component LU factorizations across 16 fine texels. Weights remain exact for that fixed set; microscopic coarse-boundary membership seams are an explicit approximation.
lscModel.domainRule: fine texel valid iff the nearest coarse grid cell is a live observed RUM; no LSC value is generated into blankies or unfilled no-data.
lscModel.predictionRule: nearest 32 live RUMs within min(3a, 4000 m), with fallback to nearest raw RUM when fewer than 4 neighbours are available.

detrend.meaning: Used only to estimate the semivariogram; not added back during prediction.
Used only to estimate the semivariogram; not added back during prediction.

meaning.variogramTrendPolicy: Variogram estimated on second-order residuals to avoid trend contamination of the covariance model; prediction uses ordinary kriging in local moving neighborhoods, whose locally-constant-mean assumption absorbs the regional trend. In pure interpolation with moving neighborhoods this is practically equivalent to trend-model kriging, while avoiding imprinting a global polynomial misfit into the predictions.
meaning.noiseModel: Formal per-cell E/N variance is placed on the kriging diagonal. Fitted nugget is recorded only as a cross-check and is not substituted for the formal variances.
meaning.crossComponentCovariance: Not modeled for the LSC prediction. Covariance texture stores 0.0 in the E/N cross-term; Monte Carlo axes are E/N aligned in LSC mode.

pit_mode.max_camera_pitch_meaning: Operational ceiling for a below-datum pit. Above this, the datum ground naturally occludes the bowl and grazing-angle overdraw becomes disproportionate. This is a readability guard, not a scientific clipping of data.

camera_depth_test.meaning: The normal 8x far-plane keeps depth precision stable. From 60 degrees pitch to the configured maximum pitch, the far-plane rises smoothly to 16x to retain distant below-datum geometry without permanently degrading depth precision.

component_bridge.note: Shortest 4-neighbour corridors only. Candidate corridor cells must satisfy the live-neighbour IDW eligibility rule.

playback_speed.meaning: Multiplier applied to playback_epochs_per_second. The epoch axis and deformation data remain unchanged.

basemap.bw_meaning: Soft low-contrast B/W reference map used by context-cap mode. It is intentionally not a Toner-style high-ink basemap.

context_cap.meaning: The B/W atlas is mapped from the true geographic UV of each fixed cap corner and moves vertically with the RUM. It is not a transparent window onto the screen-space basemap. Live context mode adds a transparent deformation-colour veil. Blankies always retain the B/W texture with a grey support veil; walls remain ordinary deformation/support colour. Context texture detail is automatically selected from a fixed overview/focus atlas pair.
context_cap.uv_mapping: four fixed cap-corner lon/lat positions projected to Web Mercator study-atlas UVs; one atlas-level V flip; no per-RUM affine UV transform
context_cap.atlas_sampling_meaning: Each fixed atlas uses DeckGL/luma linear mipmaps for clean minification and anisotropic sampling at oblique views. Atlas B adds close-inspection source detail only after the configured focus threshold. This remains a fixed study-area texture system, not live cap tile management.

atlas_lod.meaning: Automatic two-atlas cap-texture LOD. Atlas A is the existing full-study overview atlas. After the map zoom reaches focus_enter_map_zoom, Atlas B lazily builds once over the same fixed study extent at higher source zoom, then replaces Atlas A only after it is ready. Returning below overview_return_map_zoom restores Atlas A. The gap is hysteresis; no per-zoom swaps or live cap tile lifecycle are used.

two_d_analysis.meaning: A flat north-up analysis plane for reading long-term vertical velocity together with horizontal particles and glyphs. Observed RUM fills are semi-transparent and retain a subtle boundary so the selected basemap remains readable; Soft B/W is the recommended default 2D analytical background, while Map and Satellite remain user-selectable. Epoch-dependent vertical displacement, vertical uncertainty relief, walls, datum apron, and interpolated support geometry are intentionally absent.
